anomalies.observed: On the root sheet, Q2 (BC817 NPN) has pin 3 (collector) wired directly to the +5V rail, pin 2 (emitter) wired directly to GND, and pin 1 (base) on the Q_PMC_GSD net (driven from the MCU PWM line via R2 and pulled up by R1). Q1, by contrast, is correctly wired as an open-collector switch (collector to the pulled-up Q_PMC_GSD net, emitter to GND).
anomalies.expected: In an ATtiny fan controller the PWM transistor must sit in series with the fan load (e.g. collector/emitter across the switched fan-power path such as VCC_OUT), so that driving the base chops the fan current. A BJT must never have its collector on one supply rail and its emitter on GND, because that path has no load in series.

evidence.quote: Q2 BC817: pin 3 -> +5V, pin 2 -> GND, pin 1 -> Q_PMC_GSD (with R1 10K from VCC to Q_PMC_GSD and R2 1K from PWM to Q_PMC_GSD), sheet /, page 1

anomalies.impact: Whenever Q_PMC_GSD is driven high (MCU PWM high and Q1 off), Q2 saturates and creates a direct short from +5V to GND, causing overcurrent, potential damage to the supply/regulator and the MCU PWM pin, and defeating any fan-speed control.

parsed.summary: The drawing shows Q2 (BC817) wired with its collector on the +5V rail and its emitter on GND, so a high base drive (Q_PMC_GSD) shorts the supply to ground; this is the only anomaly found and it would make the board behave very differently from an intended ATtiny fan controller.
